utterances.text: I think that would be enough. Employed and charged with performing of certain duties. Maybe this is -- this is a prejudiced definition, but this is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you know, Mr. Selimi, that in fact that wasn't the definition used of collaborators by the KLA during 1998; right? You know that the definition was much broader than that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would help me greatly if you recall me what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm asking you. You're not aware, sir, of people being accused during -- Albanians being accused during 1998 of collaborating simply because they were friendly with Serb authorities or Serbs in their village? You're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, and I wouldn't agree to that definition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand you wouldn't agree to that definition because it would be improper, but my question is: Aren't you aware that in 1998 there were many instances of Albanians being suspected of collaborating because they were friendly with Serbs? You know that, don't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may have been suspicions, but suspicion is not a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And people were detained on the basis of those suspicions. Albanians -- Albanians were held in prisons. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the Albanians were fighting against Serbia. The Albanians were not being imprisoned by the Albanians. They were fighting against Serbia, against Serbian repressive apparatus and forces. Sir, your definition don't seem fair that the Albanians were being imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you aware of any instance of 1998 of an Albanian being imprisoned by the KLA for collaboration, being suspected of collaborating?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall any specific case. There may have been any instances, but I don't remember, but not imprisonment. I mean, not send someone to prison, because the KLA did not have any prison facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you say that, what do you mean by "prison facility," just so we're clear, just so the record is clear here. You said the KLA department have any prison facilities. What do you mean by "prison facility"?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may repeat it, that the KLA was not a place which could be defined as a prison, because I think all of us means what -- understand what a prison is. We didn't have such facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's be sure we all understand what a prison is. If I define a prison as any building or place where somebody is held against their will, do you still maintain that the KLA had no prisons or people were held during 1998?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am repeating it. The KLA didn't have any prisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you accept my definition of a prison when you give that answer?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to accept my definition that the KLA didn't have any prisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what's your definition of a prison?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A prison is a facility and an establishment. I think it would be naive on my part to explain to you what a prison is. I believe it's a place where people are taken, detained for long periods of time, something like this more or less. But this is not the focus of my knowledge. I don't have much knowledge on prisons because I've never been to prison, to a prison. I don't know what they're like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified earlier that you never during the war, during 1996, 1997, 1998, you never targeted Serb civilians; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm giving you an accurate definition. We never targeted armed Serb civilians. Excuse me, unarmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, do you remember after the war giving an interview to the BBC that was used as part of a documentary?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You remember that interview? You remember that programme was broadcast in January of 2003?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the accurate date, but I do remember the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you truthful in the interview?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a little clip from the interview which was broadcast, and what I'm going to do is I'm also going to provide you with a transcript of what you say in the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the usher could provide the witness -- it's been provided to the Court and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, if you would watch carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could switch to the Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, just so it's clear, on the tape the narrator on the tape will speak in English, and then most of the rest of the tape will be Albanian in English, and then most of the tape will be Albanian speaking with subtitles. The subtitling for this particular witness's portion of the interview is incomplete. It's more brief than what is actually said, which is why we have provided the transcript, which is a complete transcript of what the witness said. So if we could now play the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: NARRATOR: "A small group of Kosovo Albanians responded by setting up the Kosovo Liberation Army, the KLA. In 1996 they set out to attract the world's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: NARRATOR: "One of the grenade throwers was a law student in Kosovo's capital, Pristina. [Albanian spoken]"

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So, Mr. Selimi, when you testified here that you never targeted Serb civilians, that was not true, was it?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That was not a target. That was not the goal, to kill Serbian civilians or civilians at all. If you remember, nobody was harmed, civilian or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi --

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message was something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's be clear on what you did here. The target was the medical centre where Serb refugees were being held; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the medical centre, a school, a school of medicine. It used to be a school of medicine. Within this facility there were Serb civilians. And please let me finish, if you please. And the grenade was thrown not at the building but far, much away from the building. And the message that we wanted to convey through this, if you allow me to explain, is this --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The message was to scare the civilians out of Kosovo, wasn't it, Mr. Selimi?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message was that the Serb colonisers who had settled in Kosova was that they have come from a previous war to another war. The message was not to intimidate them but to make them aware of the situation, of the fact that they were colonisers. They had suffered other grenades before coming there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I see. You thought you would make them aware that they were colonisers, and you would not intimidate them by throwing a grenade at the building where they were staying. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was not thrown at the building, the grenade, it was thrown away, much further from the building. If you have the report compiled by the Serb police. And that grenade exploded. It was very far away from the civilians. It was very easy for us to throw it at the building, but we didn't do it. We didn't throw any grenades at the building during that night because that was not the only action taken that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, even accepting what you're saying here today that it wasn't thrown at the building, it was thrown far from the building, the purpose was to frighten and scare the Serb civilians, to send them the message to get out of Kosovo. Right, Mr. Selimi?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to scare them, to make them aware of the fact that they were foreigners in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you explain to us how throwing a grenade at or near the building where they were living, at night, would make them aware of anything except of fear?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do interpose because that's twice that Mr. Whiting has misconstrued or misinterpreted the words of this witness in relation to where it was that the grenade was thrown. He said twice it wasn't at the building but far away. If the Prosecution have material such as the Serb police report, then we would like to know if his question is based on some other information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Whiting, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, let's put aside where exactly the grenade was thrown. Can you explain to me how a grenade would do anything but frighten the people in that building, civilians in that building?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating. The aim was not to scare or intimidate people but to make them aware that they didn't know where they had come. If you allow me to go on. We couldn't do that. We couldn't make them aware by sending them letters or by begging them. They should thank us for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, they should thank you for the grenade?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, for making them aware. We warned them that sooner or later the war was going to break out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that they were in danger; correct? That's what you were trying to make them aware of, that they were in danger.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that you would believe me if I said they would be Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. most welcome to Kosova and that we would embrace them for coming there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If that's -- if that's true, that you would embrace them for coming there, then why did you throw a grenade to send them a message or make them aware, as you say?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This message was not meant only to be conveyed only at those people. It was meant also to be heard by the Serb policy which continued to send columns and -- to Kosova from Croatia and it was a message to all who were working for the colonisation of Kosova. In this case it was a message for the Serb policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when I asked you the question earlier whether you had ever targeted Serb civilians, did you forget about this event or did you just think this was not targeted Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have to understand one thing. If we targeted the Serb civilians, then there will be casualties there. I repeat, nobody was harmed. That's why I'm saying that they -- the Serb civilians were not the target of the attack. We didn't intend to cause harm to any Serb civilians that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just to make them aware.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you need me, I may repeat the same things I said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I don't need you to repeat. You met Fatmir Limaj in 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, what's your memory? What's your best memory?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Fatmir Limaj during the time when we started at the same university in different faculties. At that time, we were both students. I met him in his apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: He joined the KLA in August of 1996; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would define it a little bit differently, if you allow me. He was in contact with the KLA, and since 1996, he was more informed of the existence of the KLA, but he did not any -- perform any activity that would make him a member of the KLA at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: During 1996 did you participate in any actions with Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actions? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he provide any assistance to you or other KLA members during 1996?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to his house, and that was an assistance for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You testified that during 1997, you said, "I didn't have accurate knowledge as to where Fatmir was in 1997, and there was no way how I could because I was in such circumstances that I couldn't know. After his return from Switzerland, I realised that he was there." Do you remember testifying that way yesterday -- or, rather, on Friday?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately it was like that, but in the end of the sentence I said that I was sure where he was before he returned and after he returned. So in other words, before he returned from Switzerland, I knew that he was in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I did find out through someone. I found out that he was in Switzerland and he was active in the Fatherland Calling Fund, and I was very glad to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you have any communication with him during 1997?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attempted to establish a contact with him while he was in Switzerland in 1997. I don't know whether he got my message, but I did try to contact Fatmir while he was in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Selimi, have you been following this trial? Have you been watching the testimony of this trial?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time, parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you watch any of the testimony or cross-examination of Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, weren't you in the gallery during some of the testimony and cross-examination of Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day, yes, but not throughout his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's turn to 1998. You talked earlier today, and I'm referring to page 3 of the transcript from earlier today, that one of the biggest events that affected the organisation of the KLA was the events at the beginning of March 1998. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And up to that time the KLA had what you described as a horizontal structure; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to be helpful in informing you about the structure of the KLA at that time, and that's why I thought a definition of that structure as a horizontal one would be most appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And after the events of early -- end of February, early March 1998, there was an enormous influx of new soldiers into the KLA; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You couldn't still call them soldiers. They were Albanian volunteers who were asking for uniforms and weapons to join the KLA army because the KLA was the only force now after the attack that it had launched against the Serbian police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. Volunteers to the KLA, an enormous number of volunteers to the KLA after the beginning of March 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time we can say that it was the enormous flux of people who wanted to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And at that time the structure changed from a horizontal structure to a more organised chain of command; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because we cannot say changed. If we say that this changed at that time, it would mean that it changed at a certain point in time. At that time, the reorganisation of the KLA required time. Maybe it had begun, but it did not have the form and the structure that we desired.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But the change began after the beginning of May. That's when the change started in the structure; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends where.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, one of the first things that was done was to create operational zones; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that there was something else prior to the creation of operational zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Which was?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reception of those people and providing them with accommodation in the places where they were arriving; gathering of supplies, assistance, suggestions here and there, because we were not able to create a structure before receiving people who should have been part of that structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. You received people, and you got to work on creating operational zones. Right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be so approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And certainly by May of 1998 the operational zones that you talked about were conceived of, that is the Drenica zone, the Pashtrik zone, the Dukadjin zone and the others; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: There was no plan by May of 1998 for these operational zones?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May 1998 the creation of the Drenica operational zone began, and the organisation of the command of this zone in the existing circumstances. I say "the existing circumstances" because the circumstances were such that it was difficult for us to create a zone. However, we needed to create a structure in accordance with the existing circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Maybe you misunderstood my question. My question was: By May of 1998, you had already figured out what the Pashtrik zone was, the Dukadjin zone, the Drenica zone.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had not envisaged which would be the Dukadjin or Pashtrik zone. What we thought was that we should begin with the creation of the first zone and then with the other zones. So the first zone was the Drenica operational zone. However, we did not make precise the names, specify the names of the zones. And what those zones were going to be, we decided on that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you saying that in May of 1998 the only zone that was conceived of was the Drenica zone?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there were different ideas, but at the time, as for Drenica zone, you can say that the command of this zone was structured.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the --

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the zone was delineated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the command. I'm just talking about the existence of the zone. By May of 1998, it was already understood where the Pashtrik zone was, the Dukadjin zone, the Drenica zone, the Llap zone.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already understood where or where to continue with the restructuring of the KLA, but you couldn't know what the name of that zone would be. At least this is how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'm not making a distinction here between zones and subzones. Right. It's not an issue about zones and subzones.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference between zones and subzones was most of the time a distinction in terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Prosecution Exhibit 49, please. We actually have did in big format. And I draw the Court's attention to Prosecution Exhibit 48 at U0038566.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, I want to draw your attention to the top of the page there. You see this is a page from Koha Ditore from the 13th of May, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think it would be easiest with the witness just looks at the document and we have on Sanction the English translation of the document. It's 8573. My apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, you see this is a communique from the KLA dated -- and it's the 13th of May, 1998. Do you see that in the first paragraph it reference to the operational subzones of Drenica, Erenik, Dukadjin, Pashtrik, and Llap?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. I think you mentioned Erenik zone as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, that's there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you should know that there has never been an Ereniku operational zone in the structuring of the KLA. Let me tell you that at that time, it was an idea, a plan, and this shows clearly how it was changed later on and how it wasn't applied in the future, because the Ereniku zone was never structured.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But there's certain reference -- let's put aside the Erenik reference there. There's certainly reference to the Dukadjin, Pashtrik, and Drenica zones; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dukagjini is a province, part of Kosova. Also Drenica is a province, a part of Kosova. And as a result, maybe this was found just to be applied in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, in fact, if you look more carefully at the communique, there's reference to actions that took place in these various zones -- subzones. There's fighting in Drenica, fighting in Pashtrik. Military operations in Dukadjin. Take a moment to look at it. So you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that by May of 1998 these were actual places, the Pashtrik zone, subzone, the Drenica subzone? They're being talked about here in this communique.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree they are talked about in this communique, but the KLA in its terminology used the term operational subzone, and I suppose you have heard it quite often, and this belongs more, I think, to the earlier organisation which we described as guerrilla organisation composed of small groups operating in given zones. As to the way the people who have drafted this communique have thought, I can't tell for sure. I am here to testify to the truth, to bring you closer to it, to tell you that we have never had a full restructuring of the KLA as it is said here. I don't recall this communication and the time it was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The operational zones were a change from the earlier organisation; right? It was an effort to structure the KLA in a different way; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the time we are talking about, the summer of 1998, we were not the only ones to dictate the circumstances and the restructuring of the KLA. We were dictated also by the circumstances, by the situation. The events that occurred during the summer of 1998 and later imposed it on us to follow the events with the reorganisation of the future structure. So I am repeating that we started with the organisation of Drenica operational zone, and in May we had the code for that zone. And then we continued in August, September, with the Pashtrik and Dukadjin operational zone which happened at the same time to go on with the restructuring of the KLA until the end of the war with establishment of the Karadak operational zone. It was a procedure that took time, especially given the fact that we were in the wartime and the difficulties were greater.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: These structures were created gradually, is that what you're saying? Over time?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The structure was created in extremely difficult situation and of course it is understandable that it would take a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: They had -- these structures had to be built over a period of time.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to be built.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You couldn't just in one day have a structure, just decide that you were going to have a structure and there it would be; correct? Right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the operational zones or subzones, and I'm not making a distinction here, the -- they were created along strategic lines. The borders were created along strategic lines, not municipality lines; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually the zones are created along geostrategic lines. It depends where. In some cases they were created on the basis of the municipalities, in some others not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to March of 1998 when Fatmir Limaj came to Likovc. How long had you been in Likovc before he arrived?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Drenice, I think I'd been there for quite some time, specially during 1997 and the beginning of 1998 because I was involved in several activities related to the KLA at that time. Generally I spent most of my time in Drenice, in Likovc or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were -- around this time, March of 1998, were some of -- was Muje Krasniqi in Likovc at any time?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What about Ilaz Kodra?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He too. He may have been there several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Ilaz Derguti?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also has been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall, by the way, meeting -- seeing Ymer Alushani in Likovc?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I've seen him once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was it in Likovc?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, in Likovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. It may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Fatmir Limaj, when he came to Likovc, he came with a large group of people; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time there were other people in Likovc. There were many people, so I didn't know with whom he had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You don't remember anyone that he came with?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I'm mistaken, but he came with several people who stopped at Likovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember any of them?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sait Jashari may be one. I'm not certain. It may be Fehmi Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Lladrovci, another one. Several young men whose names I don't know. Hashim Thaqi may be the one. I don't know, but I think these were in general the people I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when he went to -- when he left Likovc, when Fatmir Limaj went to Likovc and went to Klecke, his task was to try to organise the KLA in the areas of Suva Reka, Malisheve, those areas?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think anyone had entrusted him with such a duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You don't recall having a discussion with him and with Hashim Thaqi about what he would do when he went down to Likovc -- I mean to Klecke?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly. I don't know what kind of discussion you mean, because we have met. We have discussed. We have informed each other. But I don't remember any specific debate or discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You don't recall what his task was?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the fighters had the same task. I don't think Fatmir Limaj had any specific task at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You don't think he had a task of organising in those areas, Malisevo, Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have had it as an objective but not as an assigned duty or task.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps that's a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at five minutes to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, do you remember in April 1998 Fatmir Limaj came to Likovc on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he came to Likovc, but I don't know how many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But more that once?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you went to Klecke around the end of April 1998?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that date, because Klecke was not the only place I went to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was it around that time?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In April 1998, Ramiz Qeriqi and Isak Musliu came to Likovc. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember Ramiz Qeriqi, but I don't remember that Isak Musliu came. Maybe he did come.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You remember that was in April 1998?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You remember that Ramiz Qeriqi had a letter from Azem Syla?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I said I remember Ramiz Qeriqi. I remember him because of this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And Ramiz -- when Ramiz Qeriqi left Likovc, he went to Kroimire; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where he went but this is what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: By the way, during March, April, May, June and July, did you ever go from Likovc to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, because I had no reason to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you some questions about the General Staff. You testified - and I'm looking at page 13 of today's transcript - that it was at the end of summer or in the summer of 1997 it was -- excuse me, 1998, "it was based there in Divjak." Do you remember saying that earlier today?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So your testimony is that the -- the General Staff moved to Divjak at the end of the summer 1998?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I went there several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Didn't the General Staff, in fact, move to Divjak or Klecka in May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your memory is that it didn't move -- it wasn't until August of 1998 or at the end of summer that it moved?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be approximately this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Approximately which way?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During summer, part of General Staff went to Divjak, but personally I was mostly focused in the organisation of the Drenica operative zone, and at the time there was fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. So during summer, part of the General Staff moved to Divjak. When during the summer?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any specific dates, because I don't think it is important, dates, hours, and so on. But in the summer of 1998, there was a need for a part of General Staff to be there. The public information department usually stayed there at that time in Divjak but not always.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand you can't remember the specific date, but what's your best memory of the month when that occurred, May, June, July, August?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be after the structuring of Drenica operational zone was completed, August, September, but it mostly stayed there in the end of 1998 and the beginning of 1999 and until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, do you remember being interviewed by the OTP on the 2nd of April, 2004?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You were interviewed -- you had your attorney present with you during that interview?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a legal advisor with me, a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You were truthful in that interview?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to -- with the assistance of the usher, I'm going to ask that you provided with a transcript of the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I believe that copies have been provided to the Court and to the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you could turn it page 43, please. And I'm just going to read, and both the Albanian and the English are there. And the question is: "Headquarters, where was that based?" And the answer: "It was depending. From March until May it was in the region of Drenica, in the zone we are discussing right now. But from this day it passed in the zone of Pashtrik. Exactly. We call the place Malet e Berishes, Berisha mountains." Next page: "In the village of Divjak, which is in the centre of those mountains." Were you able to follow that along with me, Mr. Selimi? Are you on the right page?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I'm on the right page. Could you repeat the number of the page, please. Is it 43 or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It seems to be 44 and 45 if I read it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sure the Court's correct. I have a different version. Thank you. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I apologise. On page 44. Are we on 44 now? Do you see it? The question is: "Headquarters, where was that based?" It's towards the bottom of the page. And then: "It was depending. From March until" -- and read on to 45: "In March it was in the region of Drenica in the zone we are talking about now but in this date passed in the zone of Pashtrik," and then you say, "in Divjak." And then please turn to page 48. You repeat it. You say: "May 1998 to Likovc to Divjak. I could not be exact. It was like the end of May, even though it could be June." Does that help you remember now that it moved in May, possibly in June?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I even mentioned it here as you may recall that I'm not sure about the dates, because the dates were not that important. And I say this when I attempt to inform you with the circumstances and the reality at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I understand the dates aren't important to you, but they are important to us. So we need to get your best memory about dates. And so now that you have seen your prior interview, do you remember that it was in May or possibly the beginning of June when the -- part of the General Staff moved to Divjak?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "You recall that the interviews of the KLA spokesperson were released from that location. The spokesperson was part of the KLA General Staff." In this context, I've said that, and I will continuously say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you recall that the spokesman made his -- Jakup Krasniqi made his first statement from Klecka on the 14th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thanks for reminding me but, however, I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But you accept that he moved to that area before he made his first statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Since he gave the statement from that part, because he couldn't have made a statement if he wasn't there. The spokesperson found that place like more appropriate one to give a public statement in the capacity of the KLA spokesperson. I think that he came to a conclusion that that was the most appropriate location.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier today that after May of 1998 you became the operational chief on the General Staff; that is right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately. I don't remember the date again, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And at around the same time, Jakup Krasniqi was appointed as spokesperson for the KLA; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the purpose of having a spokesperson was to -- so that the KLA communicate in a more direct manner with the public, both in Kosovo and internationally; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the role of the spokesperson, to have contacts with the public opinion inside the country and abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And his job was to convey a true image of the KLA; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: His job was to have contacts with the public opinion which was crucial in creating a vision amongst the people who wanted to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: To create a true image of the KLA; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was under his competence how to create that image, how to be more efficient in the -- in launching propaganda about the KLA warfare, which was not at all times true to the image of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So your testimony is that his job was not to create a true image but to launch propaganda? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that his duty was to make the population aware and to instigate people to join the KLA in this war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It was to reveal realistically the KLA, the image of the KLA; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Propaganda rarely has this role.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: His job wasn't to engage in propaganda, it was to reveal a realistic and true image of the KLA, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a public spokesperson, and his role was to make people join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You thought that he succeeded in revealing a public -- a realistic and true image of the KLA, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that because his role was propaganda and contact with the public opinion. You couldn't provide publicly at that time the KLA image. This was propaganda, a mechanism that created circumstances which would make people join the KLA war, and this is not in accordance with the KLA reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you turn, please, to page 37 of your interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And could we switch to the Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you see on page 37 the question: "Why did we do the public information?" You actually ask the question yourself. You say -- it's the -- it's --

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which line, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's the fourth line down in Albanian on 37.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. I'm actually going to play this part of the interview, and it's on the Sanction. It's not video just audio so the transcript will following along with the audio. So you can listen to it and follow along with the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: Why did we do the public information? Because at that time we did not have any representational people. We did not have a state representational body to represent us in front of the world. This body would have managed the contacts whether with the journalists or the diplomats. And of course at that time we did not have a country, a state or a Ministry of Information, let's say, which would back us up. So we included [sic] this aspect to be an immediate, an important one. And at the same time this -- we had a spokesperson who communicate in a more direct manner with the public, inner and external public, which at that time and later on it was referred to as a point of contact with the KLA, the spokesperson. At that time it was also a true image of the KLA, which helped also the world to know us better. Because at the same time with the development of the war we had -- we had an intention to reveal realistically our image, to inform who are we and what do we want. And I believe that we achieved our goals more or less with the institution called spokesperson."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. President Selimi, Jakup Krasniqi's job was to reveal a realistic and true image of the KLA, wasn't it? That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jakup Krasniqi's job was to make propaganda for the KLA, to have contacts with the public opinion, with journalists. And I've said it here and I will repeat it again: We didn't have the facility to manage this department, and whoever was in our place would have acted in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see in the interview that was just played that you said that "At that time it was also a true image of the KLA, which helped also the world to know us better. We had an intention to reveal realistically our image and to inform who we are and what do we want, and I believed -- I believe that we achieved our goals more or less with the institution called spokesperson"? And that's true, isn't it, what you said there? Those words are true?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even now I did not deny that. His role was to make a propaganda and to make a good image of the KLA warfare. And I believe that the KLA image was very good, and this was the aim of the KLA spokesperson at that time. I did not deny what I said earlier and what I'm saying now. As to how much he achieved his goal, I don't know. He knows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, I want to ask you some questions about Lapusnik. You know, right, that Lapusnik was taken by the KLA on the 9th of May, 1998; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure when you're saying "was taken." What do you mean by that. I don't think this is the right definition, "was taken by the KLA on the 9th of May, 1998." If you could help me with the wording, I would really be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Starting on the 9th of May, 1998, the KLA had control of the village of Lapusnik and, therefore, had cut off the Pristina-Peja road. Is that more clear?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. In May 1998, the Lapusnik gorge in this case - because we're not speaking of Lapusnik but of the Lapusnik gorge - the main road passing through this gorge was cut off in order to make it possible for another function. This main road was cut off in order to create another road which would be placed in the function of the population, civilian population, which at that time moved from dangerous zones to less difficult zones in Malisheve. This road that was passing through Lapusnik created the possibility for all those individuals and volunteers who wanted to help Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the population in Drenica with medicaments and food supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Cutting off the road also had a military purpose, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, everything that was military was in the function of the population, and it was for the best functioning of both the KLA and the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the KLA knew, before it cut off the road, knew that it would be strategically important to do that. That would be a strategic success to cut it off.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that road was cut off, it would certainly be a success. That's were the Serb placed most to the fall of that gorge. It would however be vital to the civilian population. If the Serb forces were still there, the situation of the Albanian population would be very precarious both in terms of foodstuffs and medicaments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: My question is you knew, the KLA knew the importance of cutting off the road there before it was cut off; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, the blocking of the Lapusnik gorge, the gorge towards the asphalt road, was a must, because hadn't we closed, blocked that, we wouldn't be able to circulate around that part. So the need was to circulate. That's why we cut off the road, and that was done on the initiative of the Lapusnik villagers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, did there -- there came a time when you decided where certain units would be located such as the Pellumbi unit, the Lumi unit, Celiku units?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the time came for us to decide whether to dispatch these units. We couldn't dispatch them or station them to different places because they were born there. They were formed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You looked at a map and named the different units; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have contributed to this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm not sure that was absolutely clear. You contributed in this respect by looking at a map and naming different units like the Pellumbi units, the Lumi units, the Celiku units, and designating where they were; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, it was very necessary to communicate through radio among the units that were set up in various villages, and this communication was impossible to do other than through a simple code system whereby we could identify the units that were formed by the villagers in various villages. That's why at that time I thought I contributed to the coding of the names of the units which were formed later in different villages. This was a temporary solution, because at the time, the codes were used only for a given period of time, only temporarily. So when the structuring of the KLA was being done in that area, there was no need for such codes because the units could be identified otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But you were the one who decided, using a map, where the different units were located and how they were named; right? That's how you contributed.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are making me repeat what I said. At that time, I deemed it necessary to contribute to the name of some units, especially units which didn't have a name. That's why I contributed to naming come of them, because otherwise I couldn't communicate using the names of the villages in the radio. This is to put it simply.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about what Fatmir Limaj did from -- during the period from March to August of 1998. In fact, he was during that time period coordinating units in the area around Malisevo, Suva Reka -- let's say from the Berisha Mountains down to Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the term "definition" is rather broad. It depends how you interpreter it, what you call a definition -- or excuse me, "coordination." Coordination might be any tendency to base, to rely on and to assist reciprocally. I think that Fatmir Limaj didn't want to be alone. He wanted to be coordinated with his unit, because without coordination he wouldn't be able to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: He was organising units in those areas from the Berisha Mountains down to Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that he organised the units because he didn't have the power to do that. Even for the organisation of his unit he had difficulties, let alone organising other units. He had been there for a short time by that period, and it was difficult for him to be engaged in organisation. He was called to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period from April to August of 1998.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. About this period I'm talking about. This is the period I meant. It was difficult for each of us at that time to be a true organiser or coordinator irrespective of the tendency to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand it was difficult, but that's in fact what he was doing, organising, coordinating that area; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, I'll try to provide you as much realistic information about events at that time as possible. Also me also to repeat that -- that to be at the head of the organisation work at that time was very difficult, almost impossible. The most one could do in terms of organisation was within a single unit during various fighting or operations to provide support for other units that operated in that area. So I think at that time Fatmir had two difficult things to do: one, to take care of his unit; and second, to be there to help other units in need during fighting. I think that was a lot of things -- a lot to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you just turn, please, to page 68 of the transcript. And I'm just going to play this portion of the transcript. It starts from -- if you look at page -- if you look at page 68, look at the top, it says: "In the Malisevo zones and around Malisevo --" do you see that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We need to switch to Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKER: In the Malisevo zone and the surroundings of Malisevo, were after, much, much after the organisation of Drenica, because Drenica had also started years before that to organise. And Malisevo started in April 1998. That is when they started to look for people. But what was Fatmir's role in this case? Fatmir inherited a knowledge, I mean knowing the relatives. And what did he do? He looked for people. He of course concentrated in the surroundings of Malisheva. I do not know the villages maybe now, but -- but it was so even when we communicated together. We together need to assist, to help the people in Malisheva. Was it easy or not, I don't want to take it [indiscernible] that but the field of his activity or concentration was in this kind of a [indiscernible] and he had two extreme points of his organisation starting from -- in the -- from the Berisha Mountains and going to the surroundings of Suhareke, going south from east, east, west, going south. I am referring also to the code names of the units. With regards to the fact of the name Celiku, code name Celiku of the units. Celiku in Berisha, Terpeze, Malisheve, up to the villages which I cannot remember the name but they're close by Malisheva. And all the way to the municipality building of Suhareke. The municipality of Suhareke, not the building, sorry. As much as I remember, in Suhareke it was Celiku 50. It was in this line, this role. His role was identified as the coordinator of all these units till we come to a level when these units are organised, structured in an operational zone. "So what time frame are we talking about then? "Exactly which time period. April, August 1998."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I need to make two corrections to the transcript. On page 70 when it says "he was identified as the coordinator of all of these," it should read "units." And then the next translation "Until we come to the level when these units are organised, structured in operational units" is what I understand the translation should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, you see where you said that "During this time period, April to August of 1998 he had" -- you're talking about Fatmir Limaj, "he had two extreme points of his organisation from the Berisha Mountains to the surroundings of Suhareke." Do you see that? It's on page 69.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in fact, Fatmir Limaj during this period was organising this area; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was trying to organise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And on page 70, it says: "He was identified as the coordinator of all these units." Do you see that on page 70, halfway down the page?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's true, isn't it? He was the coordinator of all these units.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to tell you that he was being identified as the coordinator of units, because there was Celiku 1, and Fatmir was Celiku 1. But each of the persons in charge of the units was responsible for the organisation of his unit. Therefore, it was necessary to have a general coordination of all the units let alone the Celiku units. Since they had the same name, they had different numbers, which sometimes were not in order. This does not imply, however, that he carried this role and this function.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You said "it was necessary to have a general coordination of all the units, let alone the Celiku units," and that is the role that Fatmir Limaj played. He was coordinating the units; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was identified to all as one of the coordinators who might contribute to the coordination and reciprocal assistance of the units in fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he was --

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he was identified that way because that is the role he was trying to play; right? That's what he was trying to do. Right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This unit was called Celiku unit number 1, and nobody could identify it as Celiku 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You're not answering the question, Mr. Selimi. The question is: You said, "He was identified to all as one the coordinators who might contribute to the coordination and reciprocal units in fighting." My question was: He was identified that way because that was the role he was trying to play. That's what he was trying to do; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be interpreted in various ways. I'm trying -- or allow me to try to clarify this issue. That's part of my role, to make you acquainted with the circumstances so that I --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you could answer the question and then give your explanation. The question was: He was identified in way in this role because that's the role he was trying to play; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now you can now explain.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time, there were many units formed in various villages of Malisheve. Each of the -- each of the units needed to coordinate with other units, and each unit had its role and tried to play its role in the coordination of the units. There was a horizontal organisation of the KLA at that time. Since there was a need to organise ourselves, they had to coordinate and defend themselves. They were units who knew of the existence of other units, and each of them tried to contribute to the coordination of fighting that broke out in different areas. This is what I'm trying to tell you. If I'm not clear, then please let me know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. Selimi. You testified earlier today that the brigade -- the 121 Brigade was formed at the end of August or September -- or beginning of September. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember because this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Selimi, it was formed no later than the beginning of August 1998, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The formation of a brigade was not something that could be done overnight. It took some time. I tried to describe it, saying end of August, beginning of September thinking that was the most realistic time for the creation of this unit. I think I am just -- if I say that that brigade was formed at the end of August and the beginning of September. I have my reservation, however, regarding August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, it was designated as the 121 Brigade. It was decided it would be the 121 Brigade at the beginning of August; right?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number 121 would be given to any brigade that would be formed following the Drenica operational zone and Brigade 41, for because each number has a certain function. I will try to explain it again. Every brigade, no matter what it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Selimi, I'm asking a very specific question, and if you don't know the answer you can just say. The question is: The area that became the 121 Brigade was designated as the 121 Brigade, named as the 121 Brigade the beginning of August; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be specific regarding dates. I don't know exactly, but whatever brigade was formed at that time would have that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let's turn briefly to events after the war. In August of 1999, you were the interior minister in Kosovo; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You were stopped and detained at a NATO checkpoint because you pointed a gun at British troops; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you detained in August of 1999 by NATO at a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which of the Kosova citizens hasn't been detained several times at NATO checkpoints. That was a common occurrence then. Me, too. I was stopped several times at checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you -- the reason you were detained was because you cocked your gun and pointed it at British troops; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Allow me to explain if you wish. I was not detained for any other reason than because KFOR was conducting a routine control on the road I happened to be passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your house was searched -- I'm sorry, not your house, but a house that was used by you and others as a meeting place was searched two days later and NATO found a submachine-gun, ammunition, radio frequency scanners, Ministry of Public Order identification cards stating that the bearers were allowed to carry weapons, confiscate people and detain people; right? That happened in August of 1999?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is more or less what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And on the 11th of August, you had to declare void those permits that had been given out to -- which allowed people to carry out arrests, confiscate property, and so forth? You had to make an announcement declaring those void; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In 2001, on the 27th of June, 2001, you were put on a blacklist by the United States government; correct?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date, but that may be the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your assets were frozen and you were barred from entering the United States, correct, as a result of that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Some of the others who were put on that list at the same time as you were, Daut Haradinaj, Rrustem Mustafa, Ramiz Lladrovci, and Sami Lushtaku. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You remember that the -- that the United States government said that that this group of men -- it believed that "this group of men had committed or posed a significant risk of committing acts of violence that have the purpose or effect of threatening the peace or diminishing the stability or security of any area or state in the western Balkans region." Do you remember that was part of the announcement of the United States government at the time? You remember that announcement?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even though I have asked an explanation from the office in Pristina they never informed me of the reason I was put on that blacklist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You didn't know you were put on the blacklist for supporting guerrilla forces in Macedonia at the time?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to explain. I was not -- I was never informed why I was included on that list. I was only informed of my superior, the TMK commander, that I was on that list, but I was never given a -- an official explanation why I was included in the list even though I had demanded it twice officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You recall that a month later or less than a month later that your house was searched and 250 rounds of ammunition and weapons were found in your house? You remember that happening in July of 2001?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two hundred fifty weapons, you're saying, or rounds of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. Two hundred fifty rounds of ammunition and weapons. I can't say how many weapons, but weapons.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons were there. They were given -- authorised to be there. They belonged to my bodyguard.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: They were seized by KFOR, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at home when that happened, but to my knowledge it was the KFOR that searched my house. They were legal weapons issued by KFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you some pictures from Exhibit -- it's Exhibit P24 in evidence in this case, and it's U0033240, 3243, and 3244. If you could look first, please, at 3240. And it's on the Sanction. Could you recognise that photo?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when it was taken?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was January 1999, if I am precise. To what I can see, it's January 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What makes you think it's January 1999?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The clothes we are wearing and the location where this picture was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was taken in Novoselle village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just so we have a clear record, could you just tell us who's in the photo?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am in the middle. To my right is Fatmir Limaj, and to my left is Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we now look at 3243, please. Do you remember when that picture was taken?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the date, but it's the winter of 1999. It may be January or February.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that's you and Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection from the background of this picture, it's the village of Lladrovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And finally, 3244. Can you tell us who's in the picture, when it was taken, where it was taken?

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I will try to remember what is the time period. It's autumn, summer of 1998, and from the background I think it was taken in Klecke. It could be in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just for the record, could you say who is in the picture, please.

utterances.speaker: REXHEP SELIMI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hashim Thaqi is in the middle. On his right is me, and on his left Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is perhaps a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before you do, may I raise one quick matter. It relates to matters I raised earlier on, namely the provenance of certain material said to be on the EDS system, and we have in fact searched that today, and as it stands at the moment, under all the various triggers that can be used - I'll specify them if necessary - that material does not appear to be on the EDS at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can only say, Your Honour, that I checked this morning that it was on the EDS. I was told it was. Mr. Younis was told it was. We have the e-mail traffic to confirm it, but of course we'll double-check and consult with Defence counsel about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'd be grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
